mainTopic: Do unclear partial vow-expressions (ידים שאין מוכיחות) count? This covers שמואל, the dispute between אביי and רבא, and whether that dispute matches רבי יהודה and רבנן on a גט.
overview: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's ruling, that a person must say 'that I eat of yours', means he holds that unclear partial vow-wording (ידים שאין מוכיחות) does not count. It answers yes: שמואל reads the משנה like רבי יהודה, who requires a גט to say clearly that it is the divorce document. The גמרא asks why שמואל would follow this minority view instead of רבנן. רבא answers that the משנה's extra word 'of yours' shows that clear wording is required. The גמרא then states a direct dispute: אביי says unclear partial expressions count, and רבא says they do not. רבא brings a source from the פסוק 'נזיר להזיר לה׳', which compares ידות נזירות to נזירות itself. The גמרא suggests that אביי and רבא simply follow רבנן and רבי יהודה about a גט. אביי answers that רבי יהודה was strict only for a גט, because a גט needs complete severance (כריתות). רבא begins to answer that רבנן were lenient only for a גט, and his reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does שמואל hold that unclear wording does not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's earlier ruling means that he holds ידים שאין מוכיחות are not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that שמואל holds that unclear partial vow-wording does not count as vow-wording?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind שמואל's earlier ruling. It suspects that he holds unclear partial wording does not make a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the person must say 'that I eat of yours' for the נדר to work. This suggests that שמואל does not accept vague wording whose meaning has to be guessed from context. The גמרא asks whether that is really his position, and step 2 answers yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggested reading)
He holds (this view)
'Handles': partial or shortened forms of a נדר
Partial wording that does not clearly show what was meant

steps.confusionAlert: Here יָדַיִם does not mean 'hands'. It means 'handles': partial words that 'grab onto' a full נדר.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel holds
that unclear partial expressions

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שמואל hold that ידים שאין מוכיחות are not valid?

steps.title: Yes, שמואל follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms the suggestion: שמואל reads the משנה like רבי יהודה, who holds that unclear wording does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. שמואל reads our משנה like רבי יהודה, who said that unclear partial wording does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes. It also names the תנא whose view שמואל is following.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not dodge the suggestion; it accepts it. The view is not new to שמואל. It already exists as the opinion of the תנא רבי יהודה, and שמואל explains the משנה according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Establishes or explains (a source) as following a certain view
Our משנה

phrases.english: Yes, Shmuel establishes it,
our mishna, as following Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: unclear partial expressions
are not considered partial expressions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, שְׁמוּאֵל מוֹקֵים לַהּ לְמַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1 with a yes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. שמואל explains the משנה like רבי יהודה, who holds ידים שאין מוכיחות are not valid.

steps.title: Source for רבי יהודה's view: the wording of a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה in גיטין, where רבי יהודה requires the גט to say clearly that the document itself is the divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: the essential wording of a גט is 'You are hereby permitted to any man.' רבי יהודה says it must also say: 'And this shall be to you from me a document of divorce and a letter of dismissal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where we see that רבי יהודה requires clear wording. It quotes a משנה about the text of a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן say 'You are permitted to any man' is enough, even though it never says the divorce happens through this paper. רבי יהודה requires the גט to say so outright: 'this is your document of divorce'. This shows that he does not rely on wording that is only understood from context.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The essential text of a divorce document
A document of divorce
A letter of release or dismissal

phrases.english: As we learned: the essence of a bill of divorce is:

steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in גיטין, where רבי יהודה requires the גט to state explicitly that it is the document of divorce.

steps.title: Why not follow רבנן instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: why push the משנה to fit the minority view of רבי יהודה when it could follow רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does שמואל strain to explain the משנה like רבי יהודה? Let him explain it like רבנן, who accept wording even when it is not clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's choice. Explaining a משנה like a single opinion is a stretch when it could follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן are the majority, and they accept vague wording. If the משנה followed them, there would be no need for 'of yours'. The גמרא wants to know what forced שמואל to pick רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Strains, forces (an unlikely reading)
The Sages, the majority opinion
Even though

phrases.english: Why does Shmuel strain
to establish our mishna as following Rabbi Yehuda?
Let him establish it as following the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין יָדַיִם מוֹכִיחוֹת?
phrases.english: that even though the partial expressions are not clear, the vow works?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי דָּחֵיק שְׁמוּאֵל לְאוֹקוֹמַהּ לְמַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation of the משנה as following רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is better to explain a משנה like the majority (רבנן), who accept unclear wording. Why choose a minority view?

steps.title: The משנה's extra word 'of yours' forced שמואל's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה itself bothered שמואל: it adds 'of yours' when it did not need to, which shows that clear wording is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the משנה was hard for him. Why does it say 'that I eat of yours' and 'that I taste of yours'? It could just say 'that I eat' and 'that I taste'! Learn from this that we require clear wording.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. שמואל did not choose רבי יהודה at random; the משנה's own wording pushed him there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is speaking to his friend, so 'that I eat' would already be understood to mean his friend's food. The משנה still adds 'of yours', so it must require the wording itself to be clear, not just the context. That fits רבי יהודה, not רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Was difficult for him
Teaches (the משנה states)
Let it teach (it should have said)
Learn from this, conclude from this
We require

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל follows רבי יהודה that ידים שאין מוכיחות are not valid. The proof is the משנה's extra word 'לָךְ' (of yours), which would be unnecessary if context alone were enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic way the גמרא reads: an apparently extra word in a משנה can show which opinion the משנה follows.

phrases.english: Rava said: the mishna was difficult for him;
why does it teach "that which I eat of yours,"
"that which I taste of yours"?
Let it teach "that which I eat," "that which I taste"!
phrases.notes: He's talking straight to his friend, so it's already obvious whose food he means.

phrases.english: Conclude from this: we require clear partial expressions.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the extra wording in the משנה shows which opinion it follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל could have explained the משנה like the majority view of רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unnecessary word 'לָךְ' in the משנה shows that it requires ידים מוכיחות, so it must follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree about unclear partial expressions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that אביי holds ידים שאין מוכיחות are valid, while רבא holds they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: what about unclear partial expressions? אביי said: they count. רבא said: they do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now openly states a dispute between אביי and רבא. It had only touched on this question in passing before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יד is a shortened or partial way of saying a vow. The question is about a יד that does not clearly show what the person meant. אביי says it still works, and רבא says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. This introduces a dispute between אמוראים.
Partial expressions that do not clearly show what the person meant
They count as valid partial expressions

steps.confusionAlert: יָדַיִם here does not mean physical hands. It means 'handles': short or partial wordings that 'grab onto' a full vow.

phrases.english: It was stated: unclear partial expressions.
אביי said: they are valid expressions,
and רבא said: they are not valid expressions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the issue raised in passing about שמואל and states it directly as a dispute between אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: ידים שאין מוכיחות are valid. רבא: they are not valid.

steps.title: רבא's source from the פסוק about נזירות
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רבי אידי. The פסוק compares ידות נזירות to נזירות itself, so both need clear wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי אידי explained it to me. The פסוק says 'a נזיר, to become a נזיר to ה׳.' The פסוק compares partial expressions of נזירות to נזירות itself. Just as נזירות needs clear wording, partial expressions of נזירות also need clear wording.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source from a פסוק to support his view that unclear partial expressions do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double wording 'נזיר להזיר' is where we learn that ידות work for נזירות at all. Because the פסוק puts ידות right next to נזירות itself, it treats them the same way. A real נזירות vow needs clear wording, so a יד must also be clear.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it to me
Compares or links two things, so they share the same rules
Partial expressions of a נזירות vow
Clear, explicit wording

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי אִידִי אַסְבְּרָא לִי:
phrases.english: רבא said: רבי אידי explained to me:
The verse says: "a nazirite, to become a nazirite to ה׳,"
It compares partial expressions of naziriteship to naziriteship itself.
phrases.notes: The doubled words 'נזיר להזיר' are what teach that partial expressions work for נזירות.

phrases.english: Just as naziriteship requires clear wording,
so too partial expressions of naziriteship require clear wording.

steps.raayaSupportSource: The הקש in 'נזיר להזיר לה׳' (במדבר 6:2) that compares ידות נזירות to נזירות, which requires הפלאה

steps.title: Is this the same dispute as רבי יהודה and רבנן about a גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אביי follows רבנן and רבא follows רבי יהודה, based on the משנה about the wording of a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree along the lines of the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבנן? As the משנה teaches: the core wording of a גט is 'You are permitted to any man.' רבי יהודה says it must also say: 'And this shall be to you from me a document of divorce, a bill of release, and a letter of dismissal.' So is אביי going like רבנן, and רבא like רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the argument between אביי and רבא is just the older argument between רבנן and רבי יהודה. This sets up the next two steps, where each אמורא tries to avoid being pinned to one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן are fine with a גט that does not say clearly that this paper is the divorce. That sounds like 'unclear wording works,' which is אביי's view. רבי יהודה demands clear wording, which sounds like רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? This introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test.
A dispute
The essential wording of a divorce document
A document of divorce

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion (לֵימָא). The גמרא is not concluding that אביי and רבא depend on the תנאים. In the next steps both of them reject being tied to one side.

As we learned: the essence of a bill of divorce is

phrases.english: a document of divorce, a bill of release, and a letter of dismissal."
Is Abaye speaking like the Rabbis,
and Rava speaking like Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה in גיטין (brought in step 3) again, this time to tie the אביי and רבא dispute to the תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the dispute between אביי and רבא simply match the dispute between רבנן and רבי יהודה about a גט?

steps.title: אביי: even רבי יהודה only requires clarity for a גט
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he can fit רבי יהודה's view too, because a גט needs complete severance. That reason does not apply anywhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can tell you: I hold my view even according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only said we need clear wording for a גט, because a גט needs complete severance, and without clear wording there is none. But did you ever hear him say this in general?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the suggestion that he goes against רבי יהודה. He explains that רבי יהודה's demand for clear wording is limited to a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must fully cut the marriage (כריתות). Unclear wording fails to do that. That special requirement is why רבי יהודה is strict about a גט. Since this reason exists only for a גט, רבי יהודה could agree that unclear partial expressions work for vows.

keyTerms.meaning: I, who said it (I can say my view even according to...)
He only said it up to here. This limits a ruling to its own case.
Complete severance of the marriage, which a גט needs
In general, in other cases

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you:
I said my view even according to Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said
that we require clear expressions
with regard to a bill of divorce,
since we require complete severance, and there is none.
But in general,
did you hear him say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 8 from אביי's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that אביי must disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's strictness comes from the special need for כריתות in a גט. It does not show a general rule against unclear partial expressions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a ruling in one area (גיטין) may rest on a reason found only in that area, so it cannot simply be carried over to vows.

steps.title: רבא: even רבנן were lenient only for a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins to argue that he can fit רבנן's view too, because their leniency applies only to a גט. His reason comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא says: I hold my view even according to רבנן. רבנן only said we do not need clear wording with regard to a גט...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now does the same thing from his side. He limits רבנן's leniency to the case of a גט. The sentence continues, and his reason comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as אביי limited רבי יהודה's strictness to a גט, רבא limits רבנן's leniency to a גט. If רבנן were lenient only because of something special about a גט, they could still agree that unclear partial expressions fail for vows.

We do not require
With regard to, in the case of

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 9: rejects the suggestion in step 8 from רבא's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבא must disagree with רבנן
